summary:
Traveling to Mars, a message to Earth can take up to 22 minutes to get an answer. ASCLEPIO is a health-monitoring software that gives astronauts an autonomous flight doctor for that gap. It connects to the crew's wearable devices, so no data is typed by hand, and builds a predictive digital twin of the astronaut's body across six physiological domains, such as bone, cardiovascular, stress and sleep. The twin forecasts how each system will evolve day by day during the mission and flags risks before symptoms appear.

An empathetic 3D AI doctor, "Dr. Asclepio", talks with the astronaut by voice or text, explains the health status in plain language and proposes concrete actions: adjusting exercise, choosing safe medication and, in a crisis such as a solar storm or renal colic, guiding the response step by step with no wait for Earth. Mental health is assessed with objective signals (cortisol, HRV, sleep, voice) instead of subjective questionnaires. If the AI service is unavailable, a rules-based engine keeps working silently.

ASCLEPIO addresses the challenge by letting astronauts evaluate and act on their own health during long-duration missions.
details:
WHAT IT DOES

ASCLEPIO is a closed-loop predictive physiological digital twin with an empathetic 3D AI doctor, built for long-duration missions where Earth can take up to 22 minutes to answer.

1) Pre-flight: the astronaut's electronic health record, mission profile and a short calibration interview (including a vocal baseline) set up the twin.

2) Digital Twin: six physiological domains are simulated day by day. A mission-day slider shows how the body is expected to evolve, and crisis scenarios (solar storm, renal colic and others) show how the system reacts.

3) Doctor: Dr. Asclepio, a 3D avatar with lip-sync, speaks with the astronaut, explains the status in plain language and issues orders: exercise changes, safe medication (with drug-safety checks, for example blocking NSAIDs when there is a risk), and a medication dispenser, and escalation steps for crises.

KEY DESIGN PRINCIPLES

- Zero manual data entry: data comes from connected devices.

- No subjective mental-health questionnaires: stress and wellbeing are inferred from objective signals (cortisol, alpha-amylase, HRV, sleep, voice).

- Deep-space autonomy: decisions are made on board, with no wait for Earth. If the AI service is not reachable, a deterministic rules engine takes over silently and a badge tells the astronaut.

BENEFITS AND IMPACT

Astronauts carry much of the responsibility for spotting changes in themselves. ASCLEPIO shifts them from reacting to symptoms to acting on forecasts, and reduces dependence on ground support.

TOOLS

Next.js, React, TypeScript, Tailwind CSS, Three.js with React Three Fiber (3D scenes and avatar), Recharts, Zod, Zustand, Web Speech API (voice), Web Audio API (vocal features), Claude API (Anthropic) for the doctor dialogue and the interview, deployed on Vercel. The physiological model is a deterministic simulation with fixed rules so results are reproducible and testable.

CREATIVITY

The 3D flight doctor that speaks, listens and acts, combined with a digital twin that predicts the future of the body instead of only reporting the present.

NOTE

This is a research and educational prototype using simulated data. It is not a medical device.
